itens.t: North Korea fires salvo of around 10 ballistic missiles toward sea
itens.r: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff reported that North Korea launched a salvo of approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea. The provocative launch comes amid heightened geopolitical tensions on the peninsula. Seoul and Washington continue to monitor Pyongyang's military maneuvers closely. The latest missile test follows other recent demonstrations of military posturing by the regime.
itens.d:
North Korea launched a salvo of approximately ten short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, on Thursday. South Korea's military announced the missile activity, with the Joint Chiefs of Staff providing updates on the situation from Seoul.

The launches mark a significant developing story in the region. Military authorities continue to monitor developments closely as further information regarding the missile trajectories and potential regional impacts emerges from South Korean defense officials.

itens.t: N. Korea builds 'military leader' narrative around Kim Ju-ae: spy agency
itens.r: South Korea's National Intelligence Service stated that Kim Ju-ae is consolidating her status as designated successor.
itens.d:
South Korea’s National Intelligence Service stated that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s daughter, Ju-ae, is consolidating her status as his designated successor. Pyongyang is increasingly portraying her as a future military leader through appearances suggesting involvement in nuclear and missile affairs.

Thursday's assessment provides a rare official South Korean confirmation that Kim’s daughter is named Kim Ju-ae. This specific name has notably never been used by North Korean state media in their official coverage.

itens.t: US, ROK defense chiefs agree to delay top-level military talks on OPCON transfer
itens.r: Defense leaders from the U.S. and South Korea postponed annual talks to early 2027.
itens.d:
The defense chiefs of the United States and South Korea agreed on Wednesday to postpone annual top-level talks until early 2027. This decision represents a setback for Seoul's ongoing efforts to assume wartime operational control over combined forces during a potential conflict.

South Korean Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul and U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth finalized the delay of the critical meetings. The postponement affects the timeline for transferring operational authority regarding U.S. and ROK forces.

itens.t: North Korea appears to test propaganda loudspeakers along border
itens.r: Pyongyang reportedly tested loudspeakers near the border, though some local officials cast doubt.
itens.d:
North Korea appears to have conducted a test of propaganda loudspeakers along its border with the South. The activity was reported from Seoul by Yonhap.

The apparent testing signals ongoing psychological operations and tensions across the heavily fortified border area between the two nations.

itens.t: SpaceX fires up Starship upper stage ahead of landmark Flight 15 test launch
itens.r: SpaceX completed static-fire tests on its Starship upper stage in preparation for Flight 15. The upcoming test flight promises significant milestones for the heavy-lift vehicle program.
itens.d:
SpaceX completed static-fire tests for the Starship upper stage ahead of its upcoming 15th test flight. The vehicle, designated Ship 42, performed a full-duration static fire using six Raptor engines while anchored to the ground in South Texas.

The testing sequence also included firing a single Raptor engine to simulate a deorbit burn. SpaceX founder Elon Musk indicated that the company aims to catch both the ship and the Super Heavy booster using the launch tower arms during the November flight, pending regulatory approval.

itens.t: Meet Apeiron, Virgin Galactic's 1st 'Delta-class' space plane
itens.r: Virgin Galactic unveiled its first next-gen Delta-class space plane, named Apeiron following a global vote.
itens.d:
Virgin Galactic officially unveiled the first space plane in its next-generation Delta line, named Spaceship Apeiron. The name was chosen through a public vote involving thousands of participants across 83 countries and six continents.

The spacecraft is scheduled for transport from its manufacturing facility in Arizona to Spaceport America in New Mexico. Engineers will prepare the vehicle for avionics software work, initial flight tests, and eventual operational missions, replacing the earlier VSS Unity model.

itens.t: Astronomers found a mysterious object beyond Neptune, and it could be a new dwarf planet
itens.r: The Vera Rubin Observatory spotted a distant icy object dubbed 2026 ED138 in the solar system's outer reaches.
itens.d:
Astronomers using the Vera Rubin Observatory discovered a mysterious icy object orbiting the sun beyond Neptune. Designated 2026 ED138, the candidate dwarf planet is estimated to be between 600 and 1,500 kilometers wide, making it large enough to be shaped into a sphere by its own gravity.

The object was found by Matthew Holman using search code developed with Kevin Napier at the Center for Astrophysics. Despite its extreme distance from the sun, the body appeared relatively bright during analysis.

itens.t: Microsoft AI study shows tool outperforming human doctors in complex medical cases
itens.r: A study published in Science revealed an AI diagnostic tool surpassed general practitioners in precision.
itens.d:
A study published in the scientific journal Science revealed that a Microsoft artificial intelligence tool outperformed human general practitioners in resolving complex medical cases. The research analyzed 300 challenging medical problems and compared the machine's accuracy against human doctors.

The system operates in a modular fashion, simulating a medical board where different AI modules handle distinct diagnostic steps from initial symptom investigation to collaborative result discussion. The tool also demonstrated advantages in speed and cost compared to conventional medical processes.

itens.t: Anthropic study reveals AI agents working at six times human speed
itens.r: Internal findings from Anthropic highlight rapid productivity gains and potential employment impacts.
itens.d:
An internal study by Anthropic revealed that the company's artificial intelligence agents operate at six times the speed of human workers. This technological advance has directly impacted hiring trends, as autonomous agents handle tasks with minimal human intervention.

Human roles are increasingly shifting toward management, such as drafting execution plans, reviewing results, and evaluating progress. Consequently, companies are reducing overall hiring while prioritizing technical professionals with expertise applicable directly to AI workflows.

itens.t: Hugo Calderano dominates Shinozuka to advance at WTT Champions Montpellier
itens.r: Brazilian table tennis star Hugo Calderano started his campaign in France with a commanding victory.
itens.d:
Brazilian table tennis player Hugo Calderano defeated Japan's Hiroto Shinozuka in straight sets at the WTT Champions Montpellier in France. After overcoming a five-point deficit to win the first set closely, Calderano secured control in the subsequent frames to advance to the round of 16.

Calderano entered the tournament following his seventh Pan-American title victory in Lima, Peru. In the next phase of the French competition, he will face the winner of the match between China's Xiang Peng and Germany's Dimitrij Ovtcharov.

Spanish long jumper and sprinter Julieta Gallego was among the victims of a fatal railway collision in Spain. The accident occurred near Urda in the province of Toledo, resulting in numerous fatalities and widespread grief within the athletic community.

Gallego represented the AD Sprint club in Madrid and placed fourth in the 2023 Spanish Indoor Sub-23 Championship. The Real Federação Española de Atletismo expressed deep sorrow over the loss of the 24-year-old athlete and extended condolences to all affected families.

itens.t: Netanyahu falls short of majority as Israel faces three possible government paths

itens.d:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's governing coalition fell short of a parliamentary majority as newly counted ballots showed a surge in support for Arab parties. With most votes tallied, Netanyahu's bloc was projected to secure 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, trailing an opposition bloc.

Turnout among Arab voters reached approximately 80 percent, significantly shifting the preliminary results. The outcome leaves neither major bloc with the 61 seats required to form a government independently, pointing toward difficult coalition negotiations.
